nodes.summary: Let $G$ be an impartial game, $p$ a position of $G$, and $R$ the set of remotenesses of the options of $p$ (the positions reachable from $p$ in one move). If $R$ contains an even number, the remoteness of $p$ is $1$ plus the least even element of $R$; otherwise, if $R$ is nonempty, it is $1$ plus the largest element of $R$; and if $R$ is empty, it is $0$.
nodes.title: Recursion for Smith's remoteness

nodes.summary: In an impartial game, the remoteness of a terminal position (a position with no moves) is $0$.
nodes.title: Smith's remoteness vanishes at terminal positions

nodes.summary: For an impartial game $G$, the remoteness $R(p)$ of a position $p$ of $G$ is defined by well-founded recursion along moves; the options of $p$ are the positions reachable from $p$ in one move. If $p$ has no options, then $R(p) = 0$.
